input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day of agreed liquidated damages on Customer for any delay in providing a dependency. That is a Customer-payable liquidated damages charge, triggered by even a minor or immaterial dependency slip and uncapped in duration, so it fails the fallback (which permits only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) and sits in walk-away territory because the daily accrual can exceed remaining contract value. No other clause creates a Customer-payable liquidated amount or early-termination fee, and the mutual cap in Section 21.1 does not cure it. We therefore take the preferred position and replace the charge with an unconditional confirmation that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties; nothing else in Section 7 or elsewhere cross-references 7.6 or retains a related payment mechanic.

proposal.summary: Remove the USD 25,000 per day Customer-payable liquidated damages and confirm Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, so we have replaced the USD 25,000 per day dependency-delay charge in Section 7.6 with a confirmation that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer. Vendor's remedies for a genuine dependency delay remain available as schedule relief and actual damages.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
